using 0.05 M copper nitrate solution at 400, 600 and 800 °C reaction temperatures
X-ray diffraction (XRD, Phillips PW 1700) patterns were obtained to determine crystalline phase of the copper nanoparticles
Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM, Jeol JSM 7000F) examinations were performed to characterize size, shape and surface morphology of copper nanoparticles
Leica Image Manager Programme was used for particle size and size distribution analysis by measuring all the clearly observed particles from the SEM images
Particle size distributions achieved by measuring of the particles from SEM images are shown in Figure 2
Figure 3 exhibits the EDS analysis of the particles produced at different temperatures and the presence of copper was confirmed

specifically cooled down with special spray-cooling techniques
life span from formerly max. 6 months to 24 months
accurate temperature controlled processing of the melting operation
almost constant temperatures during casting process
power supply of the channel inductors via a continuous adjustable IGBT-converter technology
